It’s so open for interpretation that I can’t relate to it so I can’t really fear it. And can Bran steer anybody into the future? He’s a repository of history, not a prophet. He can see what’s happening in other places currently as well, but only where there are still weir woods, which is almost nowhere in the South. So essentially that makes Bran a big MacGuffin for the characters to protect instead of an active participant in a story where he has demonstrated tremendous magical power, at the end of an arc that started with his disability convincing him he’d never be a knight and ended with him becoming a tree wizard. Which is disappointing. Give him some god damn agency. At least make him helpful in the battle — even if only in the planning stages. Telling the Northern Alliance about the Night King’s purpose was a great start in 802, but I wanted more in 803. Why is Bran just warging crows in the battle instead of warging Ghost or a dragon or fighting the Night King’s mind for control of the wights or something more interesting? Just a missed opportunity for Bran in that whole battle. And regardless of whether the Night King was killed the first time or simply driven back, one of the main themes of the show is about how if we forget history, we’re doomed to repeat it... so it really would have been more narratively and thematically satisfying (or at least more interesting and complex) if there was some key information from the past that only Bran, the keeper of all history, could access that was crucial to defeat the Night King, rather than just going through this whole story arc to start political shit between Dany and Jon. Now granted, there’s three episodes left, and this is a show that has always been narratively subversive (they killed off their movie star lead actor in season 1 for goodness sake), so there may be a way for the writers to tie the Cersei plot back to the Night King and the older lore in some interesting way. But I’m pretty worried they haven’t bothered to do that.
